decisions.reason: As a newly launched product line that builds directly on the firm's established offer and already received its own page, it is likely to be kept while the large firm uses its slack to learn about demand.

This skin and hair supplement is close to the firm's consumer-health portfolio and was actively presented as a new pharmacy product, so management would likely give it more time before judging it below aspiration.

Although its website visibility is more modest, the joint-health supplement is still close to the existing offer and a large established firm would usually tolerate short-run uncertainty rather than exit quickly.

The mushroom-based immune supplement appears more niche and uncertain, but because it still uses familiar capabilities and the firm has organizational slack, management would more likely continue than withdraw it immediately.

The generic blood-pressure medication is riskier because it is more distant from the established offer and competes in a demanding market, but the firm's pharmaceutical manufacturing and portfolio-expansion strategy make a one-year continuation still more likely than a drop.
